blocks.x: MS. : The preceeding taping was done in New York City, where I would travel to visit JC. He moved into the Marco Residence after leaving the hospital. As much as he wanted to come back to Wortsboro, he knew that New York City winters were much less severe than winters in Sullivan County, and he was so right.
In the preceeding tape, he talked about George Whiting a great deal, and I have a side note on that which I'd like to share with you. This was from one of our talks. I'm quoting him now:

Irving Berlin and George Whiting worked together on a song called "When My Wife's Going to the Country, Hooray, Hooray!" George Whiting thought a lot of Berlin, and Berlin thought a lot of Whiting. That was in 1905.
I dreamed of working with Whiting one day, but never dreamed it would happen, and later, to become a part of a guy who'd been part of another guy, if you know what I mean.

Oh my goodness, we were playing one day, "Believe it Beloved" and Irving Berlin was listening to it, and he liked it a lot. He was singing along, singing it right out, and suddenly, George said, "Come one, let's get out of here, if he can sing it, he can rewrite it!"
Well, that was in the vaudeville days.
I made about seven trips to New York City in February, March and April to interview JC. A few times we'd begin our interview, he's begin having increasing difficulty
in breathing, and requestd that we postpone it, let's do it next time. He was getting progressively worse and I was getting progressively concerned.
